quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, you are pulling against the thread. Let it go. Let it go. I will not let you fall.

success.outcome: You come up out of it like a swimmer, gasping and furious, with your hand on the arm of the chair. The Professor is pale. "Remarkable," he says, and then, more gravely, "Dangerous." You have a headache for an hour. You have also learnt that the thread has two ends.

failure.outcome: The thread breaks and you fall further than you meant to. For a minute you are neither in the study nor outside it. A voice says your name, and this time you answer. When you wake the Professor is holding your wrists and the lamp has gone out.

9C.title: The Bell That Strikes Late
9C.description: The Professor has your trance notes in his pocket-book. There is the water, the timbers, and the cold. There is also a bell, which you described without knowing you had: a deep bell, striking the hour a little late, as if the clock were slow. Jonathan says that the clock at Bermondsey has been wrong for years. Quincey says he has a cousin who can tell a church by its bell. The Professor says that the next session will tell them more, if you are willing, and that it may cost you more than the first.

options.label: Go with Jonathan to Bermondsey and look for the bell.
options.detail: A clock that is wrong is a clock someone has complained about, and there will be a record.

quote.speaker: Jonathan
quote.text: I know the street, Mina. I have signed leases for property in that street. It is a street of cellars.

options.outcome: You find the clock and the church and, in the court behind them, a cellar with a padlocked door. The Professor seals six boxes before dark. It is practical, tiring work, and it is the first day in a week that you have not felt the Count's attention on the back of your neck.

options.label: Ask the Professor to put you under again, at dawn.
options.detail: The first session cost you two hours. The second might cost you less, if you are ready.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, I would not ask. You are asking me. I shall do it, and I shall watch your breath.

options.outcome: At dawn you go down further than before. This time you see the box. It is a plain deal chest, and the lid is a little open. A white hand lies on the earth. A voice says that you are a very clever woman, and that he has been looking for someone like you. When you come up the Professor has you by the hands. You are crying.

options.label: Refuse a second trance for now, and work from the first notes alone.
options.detail: It was too easy. It was too much like being invited.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: He heard me. I am certain of it. A person who can be heard can be spoken to, and I do not want to be spoken to.

options.outcome: You tell the Professor you will hold the second session in reserve. He nods, a little sadly. You spend the day with a map and a pair of dividers, working out from the water and the timbers which of the three Thames wharves could be the one. By the time the others come home, you have it narrowed to two.

echoes.text: The sound of water against wood is in your ears, even in daylight.
You woke yourself from the trance. The thread has two ends and you have felt the other.

10C.title: The Invitation
10C.description: That night, at one in the morning, you wake with the taste of salt and metal in your mouth. The window is shut and the room is full of cold. A tall man in black stands at the foot of the bed. He is neither angry nor cruel. He says that you have been calling him, and he has come. He says that he could have taken what he wanted without being asked, and that he would rather be asked. Jonathan lies beside you, deep in a sleep that is not natural. In the passage, a door opens, and the men's voices are loud and a long way off.

options.label: Call for the Professor and the Host.
options.detail: You did call him, in the trance. You will not call him again. You will call someone who can stop him.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Courage, Madam Mina. This will hurt. I am sorry for it. Hold still.

options.outcome: The door breaks. The Count lets go of your hand and turns to meet them with something like regret. The Professor touches the wafer to your forehead and it leaves a red mark the size of a coin. When you open your eyes the room is empty, the window is shut and you know, with great clarity, that he heard every word you said to him in the trance.

options.label: Listen to what he wants.
options.detail: He is not hurting you. He is talking. If you stop him now you may not hear it again.

quote.speaker: The Count
quote.text: You are very brave. You are very much cleverer than your friends. Do you not wish to be rid of the pain?

options.outcome: He tells you that he is going home, that he is tired of London, that he has made a mistake in coming. He says he would rather have found you first. You do not answer. When the others reach the door he steps back into the corner, and the corner is simply a corner. Jonathan wakes and asks you why you are crying.

options.label: Think of Jonathan, and nothing else, until the door opens.
options.detail: It is the same trick you used at the boarding school: think of one thing, hold it, let everything else go by.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: I thought of Jonathan's hands, and the way he folds a letter. I held to it like a rail.

success.outcome: The cold withdraws. When the door goes in, the Count is in the corner, looking at you as one might look at a clever child, and then he is not. You have no mark on your forehead and no mark on your neck. The Professor looks you over for ten minutes and says that he does not understand it, which in him is a compliment.

failure.outcome: You hold the thought for as long as you can, and then it slips. He is very patient. He has done this before. By the time the men reach the door, you have said his name, and he has said yours, and what passes between you is not for anyone else to hear.

echoes.text: The cellar behind the church at Bermondsey is sealed. The Count will know.
You have seen the box, and the hand that lies on the earth. You have not told Jonathan.

11C.title: The Cost of Looking
11C.description: In the morning the Professor sits at the table with his hands flat and speaks slowly. There will be no more trances, he says, while the tie is open. It works in both directions. Whatever Madam Mina sees, the Count sees her seeing. Quincey agrees and Dr Seward agrees and Arthur, who has never been hypnotised, says that he would sooner be shot. Jonathan is silent. He looks at your hands and at the mark, if you have one, and at the window. He says that he trusts whatever you decide.

options.label: Agree to stop. Put the thread away.
options.detail: Give up the watch and the thread, and stop feeding what the Count is reading.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, you have more courage than all of us. To stop is also courage. I am glad of it.

options.outcome: You hand over the watch and the thread. The house breathes out. For two days you do nothing but eat, sleep, and read a novel that Dr Seward lends you. The pressure eases. On the third day the Professor gives you a look which says that it will not last.

options.label: Go on, but only at sunrise and sunset, with the Professor present and the Host on the table.
options.detail: At those hours he is weakest. A tool that can be used at the right moment is no longer a risk.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: At the edge of the day, with a witness and a wafer. It is a poor compromise, but it is a compromise.

options.outcome: The first guarded session is short and bleak. The Professor times it by the church clock, and you surface with a headache and the name of a town: Galatz. Quincey takes the Host and places it on the windowsill. It is a small ritual, and it makes the room easier to sit in.

options.label: Go on in secret, by yourself, in the small hours.
options.detail: You alone can do it, and you alone know what it is like. You do not need a witness. You need the dark.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: I knew it was foolish. I knew it was dangerous. I also knew that if I told them, they would stop me. So I did not tell them.

options.outcome: Three nights running you wait until the house is asleep and then close your eyes and go down to the water. You hear more each night. By the third, he is waiting for you. You tell no one. In the morning you write the details in your shorthand and tuck the paper into your Bible, and Jonathan sees you do it and does not ask.

echoes.text: The mark on your forehead has begun to scab. The Professor changes the dressing every evening and does not look at it for long.
You listened to what he wanted. You have not yet worked out what to do with it.

12C.title: The Door Closes
12C.description: For two days nothing comes. The sea does not rise in your head. The cold does not follow you from room to room. Then, on the third morning, a card is found under your door in a clear, old-fashioned hand: "Madam, I thank you for your visits. They shall cease." Dr Seward turns the card over twice and finds nothing on the back. The Professor holds it to the light. At noon, a telegram from Lloyd's says that a steamer, the Czarina Catherine, has left the Thames bound for Varna with a single large box in her hold.

options.label: Take the silence as a sign that he has gone, and follow the ship to Varna.
options.detail: He has closed the door because he is leaving. There is nothing more to learn from this side of it.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: He closes the door from the inside, so that we will think he is not at home. We will go to Varna as though he were.

options.outcome: You are on the boat train by evening. The silence in your head is almost welcome, and almost not. At the frontier the Professor says that he would rather have the sea in his ears than nothing in them. You say that you feel the same, and that you do not want it back.

options.label: Try to open the door yourself, from this side: call him, and see what he says.
options.detail: He is hiding from you because he is afraid of you. That is worth knowing.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: I did not think he was afraid. I thought he was waiting. The two feel the same in the dark.

options.outcome: You call, and for a long time nothing answers. Then the cold comes back, very gently, and a voice says, "I did not expect you so soon." The conversation is short. When it is done you are on the floor of your room with your face wet, and you know that he is on a ship in the Channel, and that he knew you were looking.

options.label: Use the silence: he cannot see you, so seal what is left of his lairs at once.
options.detail: Seal the last lairs while he cannot see you. The quiet will not last.

quote.speaker: Quincey
quote.text: If he has gone quiet, so much the better. A man who is not watching is a man who can be surprised.

options.outcome: For three days the hunters empty the last cellars. No one is bitten, and nothing is seen. On the fourth you stand together in the dusty yard of the last house with eight boxes sealed behind you, and the Professor says that there is nothing left in England that belongs to him.

echoes.text: You gave the Professor the water, the timbers and the cold. It was the first thing you have given him that he could use.
You put the thread away. The house breathes more easily when you are in the room.
Three nights alone, in the dark. You are very tired.

12C-X.title: The Dark Mirror
12C-X.description: You do not remember how you came to be sitting on the floor with your back against the bed. The window is open and the curtain is lifting in the draught. He has not touched you. He has not been in the room. But you can feel where he is: east and a little north, on water, moving. He is in a good humour. He says he has never met anyone who kept the faith so well with a person who had done nothing to deserve it. He says that there is a place for you in his house, and that he will keep it. He says that you will know when it is time.

options.label: Refuse him aloud, and write it down.
options.detail: Say it so that it is said. Write it so that there is a record.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: I said no. I said it three times and I wrote the time on the page. Whatever happens, it will be in the record that I said no.

options.outcome: You say it aloud in the empty room, and then you light the lamp and write down what he said and what you answered. The Professor reads it in the morning with a face you cannot read. He folds it, and puts it in his breast pocket, and says that it is the most important document in the case.

options.label: Keep what he said to yourself, and tell nobody.
options.detail: If you tell them, they will stop you. If you do not, you may learn where he is going.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: I knew it was wrong. I could not have said why I wanted so badly to hear him again.

options.outcome: You say nothing at breakfast. You say nothing on the train. You smile when Jonathan asks you if you are tired. Somewhere in the Channel, on a ship you cannot see, someone smiles back.

options.label: Tell him what you saw in the trance: where his boxes were and who sealed them.
options.detail: It is a lie to say you are not on his side if you tell him nothing. Tell him enough to keep him curious.

quote.speaker: The Count
quote.text: You are very clever. I shall remember this about you. It will be useful.

options.outcome: You tell him a few true things and several that are not. It is a game. You have not been so afraid since you were a girl. When it is over you feel very awake. You are not sure that you are winning, and you are not sure that he is losing.

13C.title: Varna by Trance
13C.description: The Czarina Catherine is late. The harbour master at Varna says that she is expected within the week and cannot be hurried. The Professor sets up his lamp and thread in a hotel room that smells of sardines and tobacco. At dawn and at sunset you go down together, and each time the water is a little more silvery and the sound of the timbers is a little louder. Today you can hear the gulls. The Professor writes in his notebook: land, soon. He does not write that your hands, when you wake, are shaking.

options.label: Go under at dawn and try to find out which quay he will use.
options.detail: The harbour has sixteen berths. The Professor wants one.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, if you can see a name on a wall, tell me the name. If you can see a number, tell me the number.

success.outcome: You see the quay as plainly as if you were standing on it: the grey stone, the lamp, a bollard painted with a white ring. You say the number aloud, and the Professor writes it down, and you come out of it weeping from the effort. By noon the Professor has found the berth and posted Quincey there with his rifle.

failure.outcome: You see only the water, and a man's back, and a hand moving a box in the dark. You say what you see. The Professor writes it down. It is no use to anyone, and you are sick afterwards in the basin. You have given him a long list of nothing, at a cost.

options.label: Let Jonathan sit with you while you sleep and write down anything you say.
options.detail: You will not go under. You will lie in bed with the lamp on. If the words come, Jonathan can have them.

quote.speaker: Jonathan
quote.text: I have been a clerk for six years. I can write down what people say in their sleep. I would like to be useful, Mina.

options.outcome: You sleep badly. Jonathan writes down eleven sentences, most of which are about water, and one of which is the name of a river. It is little. He did it for you. When he shows you the page you are moved to find that he has numbered the sentences.

options.label: Put the thread away and trust the map and the harbour master.
options.detail: The sea is full of ships, but every ship has a log. You can read a log.

quote.speaker: Harbour master
quote.text: She will come into berth fourteen, madam, unless the pilot has other ideas. The pilot always has other ideas.

options.outcome: You spend the morning in the harbour office, reading the logbook of every ship that has entered in the last month. By the time the Professor wakes, you have a list of berths in order of likelihood. Berth fourteen is at the top. You are wrong by one berth, but the margin is small.

echoes.text: You are on the boat train and the silence in your head is almost welcome.
There is nothing left in England that belongs to him.
You called him and he answered. You have not forgotten what he said.
The Professor carries your refusal in his breast pocket. He touches it sometimes, as another man would touch a crucifix.

14C.title: The Castle Calls
14C.description: You reach the Borgo Pass at dusk on the seventh day, with a dozen men from the villages and two waggons. The Professor chooses a flat place under a rock and lays a ring of Host in the grass around you. The horses scream. Wolves come out of the dark in a ring of their own. Three women stand on the far side of the Host, and one of them smiles at you as if you were a younger sister come home. Behind her you can feel something else, very far away and very close, calling you by name. It is gentle, as if you had left a window open.

options.label: Stay in the circle, shut your eyes and hold the iron cross.
options.detail: The Professor says it will hold. Believe it as you would believe in arithmetic.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Do not look at them, Madam Mina. They are very beautiful, and that is the whole of their argument.

options.outcome: You hold the cross until your palm is printed with it. The women call and the wolves keep their distance. Something in your mind pulls like a hook. Towards morning you stop hearing it, and at first light the ring is unbroken and the Professor sits beside you with his head bowed. He is asleep. He is, you realise, as afraid as you.

options.label: Answer the call, but stay inside the ring: tell him you are coming, and ask when.
options.detail: A call that is answered can be turned. You will not step out. You will make him think you might.

quote.speaker: The Count
quote.text: You are cold, Madam. You are tired. Come and sit by my fire. Nobody there will ask anything of you.

options.outcome: You speak aloud into the dark and the answer comes back clear. The Count's voice is gentle. He says he will have the door open at sunset tomorrow. He says there will be a place by the fire. When you finish, the women have stopped smiling, and the Professor is looking at you with a face like a man at a graveside.

options.label: Walk the edge of the ring and say the names of the people you love, one by one.
options.detail: A name is an anchor. The Count can reach into your head, but not into theirs.

quote.speaker: Jonathan
quote.text: Mina, say my name. Say it as many times as you like. I shall not mind. I shall be here.

options.outcome: You walk the edge of the Host and say the names. Jonathan. The Professor. Lucy. Arthur and Quincey and Dr Seward. Your mother. Mrs Westenra. You say them all and begin again. The call thins and breaks, and by midnight you cannot hear it at all.

echoes.text: The tie is deep. You can feel where the box is to within a hundred yards, like a tooth that aches when it is touched.
The mark on your forehead is the only warm part of you.
You have read what the voice said through you. You are choosing not to think about the last page.
The Professor has the notebook in his breast pocket. You have not asked what is in it.
The three pages are ash. The Professor mentions them twice a day, mildly.
You named the quay before the ship came in, and the Professor has not stopped looking at you since.
Jonathan's list of eleven sentences is in his pocket-book. He reads it at night.

15C.title: The Last Trance
15C.description: A little before sunset on the third day the waggons come round the bend with the Slovaks on the box and the great box of earth in the second waggon. The sun lies along the rim of the pass. Jonathan is on the near side with his long knife, Quincey on the far side with his, the Professor on the rock above with the Host in one hand and the cross in the other. You are in the middle of the road with your eyes closed, and you can feel him as if he stood in front of you. He is awake. He knows you are here. He is waiting for you to decide.

options.label: Lead the hunters to the box with your eyes closed, and stay awake until it is done.
options.detail: You are the compass. You have been the compass the whole way.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: Left of the white rock. Under the third lashing. It is the box on its side. Now, Mr Harker. Now!

options.outcome: You walk the road with your hands out like a child at blind-man's buff, and tell them where the box is. Jonathan's knife goes across the throat and Quincey's goes into the heart. The Count crumbles to dust. Quincey, cut in the side, leans on the box, smiling. The cold goes out of your head as if a door had been opened.

options.label: Have the Professor touch the Host to your forehead and cut the tie before you go any further.
options.detail: It ends his hold on you, and it ends your place in the hunt.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: I shall do it. I shall do it quickly. After this, Madam Mina, you will be only yourself. I think you will find that you miss him.

options.outcome: The wafer burns, and the tie breaks like a wire. You hear him cry out, a long way off, and the cry is nothing like a monster's. When you open your eyes you are alone in your head for the first time since Whitby. The hunters go on without you. The silence is a kind of grief.
options.requiresFlagHint: NEEDS THE HOST KEPT TO HAND

options.label: Let him believe you have come over to him, and bring him into the trap.
options.detail: He has wanted you for weeks. Give him what he wants, in the one place where it will cost him.

quote.speaker: The Count
quote.text: At last. I knew you were a woman who understood these things. Come here and let me look at you.

options.outcome: You walk to the box and kneel. The lid lifts and the pale hand comes out. You put your forehead against it, and say that you are tired and that you are ready to be his. His face, in the last light, is quite human. He is smiling. Two blades come out of the trees together. His face does not change before the dust takes it.
options.requiresFlagHint: NEEDS THE TIE TO BE DEEP ENOUGH TO BELIEVE

options.label: Go to him. Leave the circle, the cross and the men, and walk up the road.
options.detail: You have been tired for a long time. He has said there is a place by the fire.

quote.speaker: Jonathan
quote.text: Mina? Mina, come back. Mina, please. Please come back.

options.outcome: You walk past Jonathan with your eyes open and your hands empty. The Professor calls your name from the rock. Quincey does not raise his rifle. The box opens, and the Count steps out into the last of the light as if it were the least of his worries. He takes your hand, and it is warm.
options.requiresHint: OPENS ONLY TO A MIND THAT HAS OPENED ITSELF TO HIM, WITH NOTHING ELSE TO HOLD

echoes.text: Every name you said on the pass is still in your mouth.
You held the cross for a night and your palm still shows the print of it.
You answered him from the circle. He is expecting you.

13A-X.title: Questions at the Customs House
13A-X.description: The sailors walk you to the customs house without touching you. An officer in a shiny coat has your passport and the Professor's visiting card and has begun to ask, in three languages, why a party of English people wants to search a Russian steamer for a box of dirt. The Professor stands with his hat in his hands and does not say that it is a matter of the Host. The tide is turning outside. Somewhere in the harbour the box is being lifted onto a barge.

options.label: Tell the officer a plain story: an inheritance, a missing coffin, a quarrel with a Hungarian solicitor.
options.detail: A dull story with a lawyer in it. It will take an hour, and the barge will not wait.

quote.speaker: Officer
quote.text: A coffin of dirt, madam? I have heard stranger. Wait here, and do not touch the stamp.

options.outcome: It takes an hour and three cups of coffee. At the end the officer stamps your papers, apologises in two languages and gives the Professor a pamphlet on the history of Varna. You are out on the quay by noon. The barge has gone.

options.label: Put a sovereign under the blotter and ask for the officer's best attention.
options.detail: It is quicker, and the Professor is already looking at the clock.

quote.speaker: Officer
quote.text: You are a lady of great understanding. I find that I have no further questions at all.

options.outcome: The sovereign goes into a drawer. The officer remembers an urgent appointment, and a clerk takes your names in a ledger with a very ornate hand. You are out on the quay in twenty minutes. The Professor says that the best rite in the world is often a small coin in the right place.

options.label: Slip out of the side door while the Professor holds the officer's attention.
options.detail: He is an old man, and he is very good at being a nuisance on purpose.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Go, Madam Mina. I shall be arrested very slowly. I have had practice.

options.outcome: You walk round the end of the customs shed and down to the water. A boy sells you a place in a rowing boat for sixpence and you see the barge from three hundred yards, with the box on its deck under a tarpaulin. The Professor joins you at nightfall with a black eye and a good deal of dignity.

14B-X.title: A Sandbar at Noon
14B-X.description: The launch is stuck fast. The keel has found a bank of sand and gravel in the brown water, and Arthur has put the engine astern twice and then forward twice, and each time the boat has settled a little more. The barge with its four Slovaks goes by across the water at walking pace. Jonathan has the rifle, and does not use it. There is a farmhouse on the bank and, in front of it, a man with a long pole who has been watching the whole thing with interest.

options.label: Lighten the launch: coal, cases and everything that can be tipped into the river.
options.detail: The Zenobia draws two feet less without her stores. It is a good price for an hour.

quote.speaker: Arthur
quote.text: Over the side with the spare coal, gentlemen. Not the rifles. I shall be very cross about the rifles.

options.outcome: You pass cases of tinned meat hand to hand along the deck. The boat rises an inch, then three, then slides off with a long scrape. Arthur looks at the coal that is left and says it is enough for a day and a half. You do not eat tinned meat again for a year.

options.label: Go over the side, all of you, and push.
options.detail: Four men and a launch are lighter than four men in a launch.

quote.speaker: Quincey
quote.text: It is ten feet to the bank, ma'am. It is cold. I do not mind it as much as I thought.

options.outcome: The water is thigh-deep and the colour of tea. It takes eleven minutes. When the launch comes free, you are standing in the river to the waist with your skirts floating around you, laughing, and you cannot remember when you last did.

options.label: Hail the man with the pole and offer him five pounds for a tow.
options.detail: A farmer with a team of horses and a rope will have the launch afloat in a quarter of an hour.

quote.speaker: Farmer
quote.text: Five pounds, lady? For a boat? I have had a cow stuck in a worse place for nothing.

options.outcome: He fetches two horses from the barn and a rope as thick as your wrist. The launch is on the water in twenty minutes. The farmer takes the five pounds with great ceremony and asks, as an afterthought, whether you are going to the war.

13C-X.title: What the Professor Wrote Down
13C-X.description: You wake on the floor of the hotel room with a cut lip, and the Professor is kneeling beside you with his notebook. He is writing very fast, and when he looks up his face is grey. You spoke for eleven minutes, he says, and not for the whole of it in your own voice. He has written down what was said. He has not decided whether you should see it. The sash is up, and the gulls have stopped.

options.label: Ask to see the notebook, and read it all.
options.detail: If it was your mouth, it was your business.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, you are a woman of great courage. I should like you to read this sitting down.

options.outcome: You read it by the window. It is nine pages long and the first six are about water. The last three are in a different hand, or rather in the Professor's hand imitating a voice, and the voice is saying how pleased it is that you are so clever, and asking after Jonathan by name. You close the book and the Professor takes it back with both hands.

options.label: Tell him not to read it aloud, and not to tell you what is in it.
options.detail: A thing that has been said cannot be unsaid. A thing that has not been heard can be put off.

quote.speaker: Mina
quote.text: Please put it away, Professor. Whatever it says, I shall act on what I know, and not on what I have said.

options.outcome: He closes the notebook and slips it inside his coat, and you can hear that he is relieved. For the rest of the journey he is gentler with you than he has been. At night, in the next compartment, you hear him turning the pages.

options.label: Tear out the pages in the strange voice and burn them in the grate.
options.detail: If he said it through your mouth, it should not be in a book.

quote.speaker: Van Helsing
quote.text: Madam Mina, it is evidence. It may be the only evidence. I beg you to reconsider.

options.outcome: You hold the three pages in the flame until they curl. The Professor does not stop you. He watches, with the expression of a man at a funeral that he agrees with and wishes he did not. The smell of burnt paper hangs in the room until morning. Nobody mentions it at breakfast.

LORE_DEMETER.headline: A WRECK AT WHITBY: THE RUSSIAN SCHOONER DEMETER
LORE_DEMETER.bodyText:
WHITBY. A storm of unusual violence struck this coast on the night of the sixth, and on the evening tide a Russian schooner, the Demeter, out of Varna with a cargo of silver sand and boxes of mould, ran straight into the harbour under full canvas with no one at the wheel. The master was found lashed to the helm, dead, a crucifix wound in his hands. Of the crew nothing has been seen. The vessel's papers are in the care of the Board of Trade.

A large dog, said by several witnesses to have sprung ashore from her deck at the moment of grounding, has not been found. The coastguard asks that residents of the East Cliff keep their children indoors after dark.

LORE_WOLF.headline: AN ESCAPED WOLF: THE ZOOLOGICAL GARDENS ALARMED
LORE_WOLF.bodyText:
A grey wolf has escaped from the Zoological Gardens in Regent's Park. The animal, which had been quiet for months, was last seen on the night of the nineteenth, going north. A keeper who followed it as far as Primrose Hill says that it paid no attention to him at all, and ran like an animal that knew where it was going.

Residents of Hampstead are asked to bolt their shutters. The Superintendent of the Gardens wishes it understood that the wolf is old, tame, and generally a gentle creature, and that it is not given to breaking into houses.

LORE_BLOOFER.headline: A HAMPSTEAD MYSTERY: THE BLOOFER LADY
LORE_BLOOFER.bodyText:
HAMPSTEAD. Several children, all under ten, have been found on the Heath after dark during the last week, each with a small wound at the throat and each in an exhausted state. They tell the same story to anyone who asks. A beautiful lady in white spoke to them kindly, took them for a walk, and sent them home.

The children call her the Bloofer Lady. Local constables have made a number of enquiries and have found no such person. The doctors say that the wounds are no more than scratches. They have declined to say what could have made the scratches in pairs.

TRANSITION_COUNCIL.source: A Note in Mrs Harker's Hand
TRANSITION_COUNCIL.headline: THE PAPERS ARE IN ORDER
TRANSITION_COUNCIL.bodyText:
PURFLEET. The papers are in order. Jonathan's journal is typed fair. Dr Seward's cylinders have been transcribed. The cuttings are pasted, and the dates are checked against the Bradshaw. Professor Van Helsing has read the lot, twice, and has put a question mark against nothing.

What has to be done is plain, and so is what it will cost. We have a house next door that is not empty, fifty boxes in the country that are not what they appear to be, and a man who has made up his mind to stay. I am writing this at the desk in Dr Seward's study with the lamp lit. Tomorrow I shall begin the work.

LORE_CZARINA.headline: THE CZARINA CATHERINE, FOR VARNA
LORE_CZARINA.bodyText:
SAILED. The steamer Czarina Catherine, 1,200 tons, left the Thames on the morning tide for Varna, with general cargo and one consignment of earth, in a single large case, for forwarding to Galatz. The ship is reported to have made a fair passage down the Channel with a fresh following wind, and to have been seen off Gibraltar. Her master has reported no passengers.

The Varna agent is informed that her arrival is expected a day ahead of her usual time. Nobody at Lloyd's can account for the wind.

CRISIS_NERVE.headline: MRS HARKER: A NOTE ON HER CONDITION
CRISIS_NERVE.bodyText:
PURFLEET. I have been watching Mrs Harker for a week and must record that I do not like what I see. She sleeps for an hour at a time and wakes with her hand at her throat. She flinches when a door opens, and she has taken to writing in her sleep, in a shorthand I cannot read. The Professor calls it the strain, and that she is stronger than any of us.

I do not doubt it. I also know what a mind looks like just before it breaks, and I have seen a good many. I have said nothing to her husband.

CRISIS_BLOOD.headline: PALLOR
CRISIS_BLOOD.bodyText:
I have asked Mrs Harker to lie down. She is white to the lips and her hands are cold. She tells me she is perfectly well and I do not believe her, and she knows I do not, and we have agreed not to discuss it. I have seen this colour before, in a house at Hillingham, on a young woman I could not save.

I shall give her my blood if I must. I shall do it at once, without telling the others. A man who has done what I have done in his life cannot do less than this for the woman who has typed it.

CRISIS_FELLOWSHIP.headline: TO MRS HARKER, WITH REGRET
CRISIS_FELLOWSHIP.bodyText:
RING. My dear Mrs Harker, I find it difficult to write this, and I shall be brief. I have been thinking about what the Professor asked of us all at Purfleet and what each of us has done since. I do not think we are a company any longer. I think we are six people with six plans, and it is no way to catch anything.

I have put my affairs in order and I am going home for a week. You will think me a coward, and I daresay I am. If you wish me to return, send a line. I shall come.

ENDING_1A.title: The Last Sunset
ENDING_1A.headline: AMERICAN GENTLEMAN DIES IN THE CARPATHIANS
ENDING_1A.text: The sun touches the ridge as the long knife touches the throat. The bowie goes into the heart a breath later, and the Count has turned to dust before the lid has stopped moving. Quincey Morris is cut in the side and does not know how badly until he sits down. He dies at the foot of the pass an hour afterwards with his head on your arm. He says he is glad, and asks you to tell Arthur that it was no trouble. You bury him on the road to Bistritz. Jonathan holds your hand all the way down to Bistritz and says very little.

variants.headline: DEATH OF A TEXAN: THE PASS AT BORGO
variants.text: The sun touches the ridge as the long knife touches the throat. The bowie goes in a breath later, and the Count has turned to dust before the lid has stopped moving. At the same moment the scar on your forehead goes pale, and by evening there is nothing there but skin. Quincey Morris is cut in the side and does not know how badly until he sits down. He dies at the foot of the pass an hour afterwards with his head on your arm. He says he is glad. You bury him on the road to Bistritz.

ENDING_1B.title: The Burial Office
ENDING_1B.headline: A PRIEST'S SERVICE AT THE BORGO PASS
ENDING_1B.text: You read the committal from the Professor's prayer-book, and the men hold the road. When you reach the last words you hear the lid lift, and the voice in the box says a single word, and it is thanks. Nobody strikes him. The dust comes by itself, slowly, and the wind takes it down the pass. The gipsies kneel on the road and cross themselves in a manner you do not recognise. Quincey is alive, and Jonathan is alive, and the Professor says that he has never in his life been so wrong about the price of a mercy.

variants.headline: THE PRIEST OF VARNA SAYS MASS FOR AN UNKNOWN MAN
variants.text: You read the committal from the Professor's prayer-book, with the priest's iron cross round your neck, and the men hold the road. When you reach the last words you hear the lid lift, and the voice in the box says one word, and it is thanks. Nobody strikes him. The dust comes by itself, slowly. At Varna, a fortnight later, the priest says a mass for him by name. He does not ask what the name was. Quincey is alive, and Jonathan is alive, and the Professor says that he has never in his life been so wrong about the price of a mercy.

ENDING_1C.title: A Box in Holy Ground
ENDING_1C.headline: SEALED CHEST FOUND IN VILLAGE CRYPT
ENDING_1C.text: The box goes down to the village on a sledge, bound in iron and sealed with the last of the Host. The priest wakes at midnight and does not ask a single question. By morning the box is in the crypt under three feet of stone, and the priest has the only key. Nobody is dead. The Count is not dust. The Professor says that a thing sealed in holy ground is a thing deferred, and that you will have to be patient. You are not sure he says it to you. Jonathan takes your hand on the road home and does not let go of it until Exeter.

variants.headline: SEALED CHEST FOUND IN VILLAGE CRYPT
variants.text: The box goes down to the village on a sledge, bound in iron and sealed with whatever is left of the Host. There is not much. The priest wakes at midnight and does not ask a question. By morning the box is in the crypt under three feet of stone. The Professor says that a thing sealed with so little is a thing deferred by a short time, and that you will have to be vigilant. He says it to himself. Jonathan takes your hand on the road home and does not let go of it until Exeter.

ENDING_1D.title: A Look of Peace
ENDING_1D.headline: FOREIGN NOBLEMAN BURIED WITHOUT CEREMONY
ENDING_1D.text: You kneel at the box and say what you came to say. There is a long silence, and then the Count's hand touches your forehead and there is no heat in it. He looks at you with something that can only be called relief. The sun goes behind the ridge, and as the light leaves him the face in the box is the face of a man who has been very tired for a long time. He crumbles to dust, and the last thing on his face is a look of peace. Quincey and Jonathan lower their weapons. Nobody speaks until Dr Seward blows his nose.

variants.headline: THREE WOMEN FOUND SLEEPING IN A RUINED CHAPEL
variants.text: You kneel at the box and say what you came to say. There is a long silence, and then the Count's hand touches your forehead and there is no heat in it. He looks at you with relief. The sun goes behind the ridge, and he crumbles to dust with a look of peace. In the castle above, three women who have not slept in three hundred years lie down in the chapel and are found there in the morning, quite still, with the beginnings of a smile. You do not know whether you did that, or he did.

ENDING_2A.title: The Wagon on the Road
ENDING_2A.headline: FIGHT ON THE PASS: ONE DEAD
ENDING_2A.text: The Slovaks scatter at the first shot. The lid comes off under two crowbars, and the long knife and the bowie do their work. The Count is dust before the sun is off the road. Quincey is cut in the side. He sits down on the box and says that it has been a good fight, and that he is glad of it. He dies at nightfall, with Arthur holding one hand and you the other. You type his name into the record that night, first among the dead, and you do not stop typing until morning.

variants.headline: TYPEWRITTEN ACCOUNT OF A PASS FIGHT FILED
variants.text: The Slovaks scatter at the first shot. The lid comes off under two crowbars, and the long knife and the bowie do their work. The Count is dust before the sun is off the road. Quincey is cut in the side and dies at nightfall. You type his name into the record that night, first among the dead, and when you are done the record is complete: fifty boxes, one wagon, one dead American and one dead nobleman, all of it in order. Jonathan binds the pages and writes the date on the cover.

ENDING_2B.title: The River Takes the Box
ENDING_2B.headline: BARGE SUNK ON THE SERETH: BOX NOT RECOVERED
ENDING_2B.text: The box goes down with a sound like a door closing. Arthur lets out the chain. Nothing comes up, then or later. You stand on the deck of the launch until the ripples have all gone out to the banks. No one is hurt or dead, and the Professor says the river will keep what it is given for as long as it is a river. Dr Seward writes to a friend at the Danube Commission and asks, very mildly, whether anyone proposes to dredge the Sereth. He is told that nobody does.

variants.headline: A LAUNCH CLEARS A RIVER NARROWS
variants.text: The box goes down with a sound like a door closing. Arthur lets out the chain. You were three bends ahead of the barge at the time and had two hours in hand, and when it was done you had four hours to wait for dusk on the bank. Nothing comes up. No one is hurt. The Professor says the river will keep what it is given as long as it is a river. Dr Seward writes to a friend at the Danube Commission and asks whether anyone proposes to dredge the Sereth. Nobody does.

ENDING_2C.title: The Sealed Hold
ENDING_2C.headline: CUSTOMS SHED INCIDENT AT GALATZ
ENDING_2C.text: The harbour master asks what the powder is. The clerk, writing, says that he supposes it is the packing. The box is opened in the presence of two witnesses and the seal is broken in daylight, and nothing has to be cut. You sign the report as a witness. In the margin the harbour master has written, in careful English, that the consignment was unfit for transit. It is a good deal better than anything that was said at Whitby. The Professor shakes your hand outside, in the sun, and tells you that this is the best day's work in the case.

variants.headline: TELEGRAMS FROM LONDON EXPLAIN A CUSTOMS SEIZURE
variants.text: The harbour master asks what the powder is. The clerk, writing, says that he supposes it is the packing. The box was opened under a seal that you arranged by wire from London, three weeks and twenty-six telegrams ago. You sign the report as a witness. The Professor shakes your hand outside, in the sun, and says that he has spent forty years looking for an enemy that could be defeated with a stamp. The harbour master asks him whether he would like a receipt.

ENDING_2D.title: The Last Dispatch
ENDING_2D.headline: FOUR PARTIES MEET AT A BRIDGE: ONE NOBLEMAN DEAD, NONE INJURED
ENDING_2D.text: Not a man is wounded. Both blades go in together, in perfect time, and the Count has turned to dust before the sun has left the road. The four parties had arrived within a minute of each other from four directions on a road with no signposts, and when Quincey is asked how, he points at you. "She said the fourteenth bridge," he says. "It was the fourteenth bridge." You file the account in triplicate. The Professor frames one copy. Your son, born the following year, is given all their names. He is told about this at bedtime, and grows up thinking that timetables are the stuff of legend.

variants.headline: A PLAIN MAN IN A BOWLER HAT PAID IN FULL
variants.text: Not a man is wounded. Both blades go in together, and the Count has turned to dust before the sun has left the road. The four parties arrive within a minute of each other, and an inquiry agent in a bowler hat, who has been following the carters for three weeks, watches from a hedge with a notebook. You pay him afterwards. He asks no questions. He never discovers what he has been paid for, and his notes are sold for waste paper in 1923.

ENDING_3A.title: The Compass Held
ENDING_3A.headline: WOMAN'S EVIDENCE LEADS TO DEATH ON THE PASS
ENDING_3A.text: You walk the road with your hands out and your eyes closed and tell them where the box is. Jonathan's knife goes across the throat and Quincey's goes in at the heart. The Count crumbles to dust, and the cold goes out of your head as if a door had been opened. Quincey sits down on the box and does not get up. You hold his hand until the end. For years afterwards you will wake at dawn and sunset, and reach, and find nothing there. You are not sure whether that is grief for Quincey or for the other.

variants.headline: A WIFE'S SECRET, KEPT TO THE LAST
variants.text: You walk the road with your hands out and your eyes closed and tell them where the box is. The knives go in, and the Count crumbles to dust. The cold goes out of your head. Quincey dies at the foot of the pass. Jonathan has your hand, and he asks you at last what you left out of the trance, the first night. You tell him. He does not let go. He says it is smaller than he feared and harder to bear than he thought. He does not let go.

ENDING_3B.title: The Scar and the Silence
ENDING_3B.headline: SCARRED WOMAN RETURNS FROM TRANSYLVANIA
ENDING_3B.text: The wafer burns, and the tie breaks like a wire. You hear him cry out, a long way off, in a voice that is nothing like a monster's. You open your eyes in the road and you are alone in your own head for the first time since Whitby. The hunters go on without you, and they come back at dusk with the news that it is done. Quincey is dead. The Count is dust. The scar on your forehead stays, the size of a coin. You wear a hat with a brim for the rest of your life, and Jonathan never once asks you to take it off.

variants.headline: A SCARRED WIFE, UNEXPLAINED
variants.text: The wafer burns, and the tie breaks like a wire. You hear him cry out, a long way off. You open your eyes in the road and you are alone in your own head for the first time since Whitby. The hunters go on without you, and they come back at dusk with the news that it is done. The scar on your forehead stays. You wear a hat with a brim for the rest of your life, and you tell the Professor, years later, that you wish you had taken the Host on the first night. He says nothing, but he takes your hand.

ENDING_3C.title: The Lure
ENDING_3C.headline: WOMAN FOUND KNEELING AT AN OPEN CHEST
ENDING_3C.text: The pale hand closes on yours, and for one moment you are afraid that you have made a mistake. Then the long knife and the bowie come out of the trees together, and the Count's face does not change before the dust takes it. You are on your knees on a mountain road with the remains of a man several centuries old on your sleeve. You have never before been so tired and so awake. Jonathan lifts you. Quincey has a long cut in the side and does not mention it. Dr Seward is sick behind a rock. The Professor, very quietly, says that you are the most terrible woman he has ever had the honour to know.

variants.headline: A CUNNING WOMAN, AND WHAT SHE FED A CHEST
variants.text: The pale hand closes on yours. For one moment you are afraid, and then the long knife and the bowie come out of the trees together. The Count's face does not change before the dust takes it, and in the last second you see that he is smiling at the lies you fed him in the dark. He had known them for lies. He had liked them. You kneel on the road with his dust on your sleeve and the knowledge that the best conversation of your life has ended. The Professor says nothing at all.

ENDING_3D.title: The Bride of the Dark
ENDING_3D.headline: MRS HARKER MISSING FROM PASS: SEARCH ABANDONED
ENDING_3D.text: You walk past Jonathan with your eyes open and your hands empty. The Professor calls your name from the rock. Quincey does not raise his rifle. The box opens, and the Count steps out into the last of the light as if it were the least of his worries. He takes your hand and it is warm. The sun goes behind the ridge. You walk up the road beside him, and the castle is lit. The men are left in the road with their weapons in their hands. Jonathan sits down in the dust. In the typescript, the last page is blank.

variants.headline: A PRESCRIPTION, AND WHAT BECAME OF IT
variants.text: You walk past Jonathan with your eyes open and your hands empty. The Professor calls your name from the rock. The box opens, and the Count steps out. He takes your hand, and it is warm, and the sun goes behind the ridge. In your pocket there is a bottle that the Professor gave you at Hillingham, and you hold on to it until the gate, and then you let go. You did not take the remedy in time. The men are left in the road. In the typescript, the last page is blank.

ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.title: The Padded Room
ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.headline: MRS HARKER REMOVED TO THE ASYLUM AT PURFLEET
ENDING_CRISIS_NERVE.text: It is the small things that go first: the typewriter, the hour, your own signature. You stop answering to your name. Dr Seward looks at you across a table in his own study, with his own cylinder-machine running, and tells the phonograph that it is a case of acute mania following exposure to extreme horror. He puts you in Renfield's old room. It is clean. There is a window, and somebody has left a small box with a spider in it. Jonathan visits on Sundays. He reads aloud from the typescript, which he has bound, and which you can no longer recognise as your own.

ENDING_CRISIS_BLOOD.title: The Last Entry
ENDING_CRISIS_BLOOD.headline: DEATH OF A YOUNG WIFE: NO CAUSE ASSIGNED
ENDING_CRISIS_BLOOD.text: You have given too much and kept too little. At Hillingham, at Purfleet, on the road, and in the dark with a stranger's hand at your neck. The Professor takes your pulse at dawn and says nothing. At noon you sleep, and at four he does not wake you. The coroner's report says anaemia and nervous exhaustion. Jonathan tears it up. In the typescript there is a last entry in your shorthand, made on the morning before: a list of the boxes still at large, with the numbers and the addresses, and, in the margin, the word 'sorry'.

ENDING_CRISIS_FELLOWSHIP.title: Every Hand Alone
ENDING_CRISIS_FELLOWSHIP.headline: SOCIETY OF GENTLEMEN DISSOLVES: THE COUNT AT LARGE
ENDING_CRISIS_FELLOWSHIP.text: By the end of October the party that met in Dr Seward's study has gone its separate ways. Arthur is at Ring, putting his father's estate in order. Quincey has gone back to Texas. Dr Seward has taken a post in the north, and the Professor is in Amsterdam, writing letters he does not send. Jonathan is in Exeter, at Mr Hawkins's old desk, and you keep the typescript in a locked drawer. Somewhere in the Black Sea a steamer is making good time with a single box. Nobody is at the quay in Varna to meet it. Nobody at all.
